findings.title: Recovery codes are written to user storage as raw plaintext codes
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes `generatedCodes` (the raw, unhashed codes shown to the user) and passes that JSON as the credential data to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. The local DB path stores only hashed codes (via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel). Storing the raw secrets in an external user store (LDAP, custom federation) is inconsistent with the local path and leaks reusable secrets to a system Keycloak does not control. The stored form should be the same hashed form used locally, with verification hashing the input (RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode).

findings.title: Recovery codes validated in user storage are never consumed and can be reused
findings.body: In isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE the code is only checked with `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...)`. Nothing marks the used code as consumed or removes it, so the same recovery code can be used to log in unlimited times. The local path tracks used codes and removes the credential once all are used (see RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.action). The federated path therefore silently breaks the one-time semantics of recovery codes. The test only covers a single successful login and does not catch this.

findings.title: Removing an exhausted recovery credential only targets the local store
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential may return a credential that lives in user storage (federated). When all codes are used, the code calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(id)`, which only operates on the local DB. For a federated credential the removal does nothing, so the exhausted credential remains and the user is not forced to reconfigure correctly. The removal should go through the credential source that actually owns the credential, or the federated case should be handled explicitly.

findings.title: getCredentials dereferences myUser without a null check
findings.body: getCredentials calls getMyUser(user) and immediately accesses `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp`. If the user is not present in the map (getMyUser returns null), this throws NullPointerException. Other methods in the same class (isConfiguredFor, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream) guard against null.

findings.title: Test does not verify one-time use or regeneration of recovery codes
findings.body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only logs in once with code 0. It does not check that the same code is rejected on a second login, that used codes are consumed, or that regenerating codes replaces the previous set in user storage. Those are the behaviors most likely to be broken by the federated implementation, as the isValid path shows.

findings.title: Helper takes a delay parameter that is always 0 and has a misspelled alias
findings.body: configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes accepts `long delay` but the only caller passes 0, so the parameter is dead flexibility. The config alias "delayed-suthenticator-config" is misspelled, which is confusing if it is ever referenced by name.
